text:
Alex: proposing a new lightweight evacuation workflow for GPU nodes triggered by multi-signal health voting. want to avoid brittle hard-drains during transient Xid/ECC bursts.
Priya: yes please. current autodrain is too binary — we either keep a node or nuked it. what's the high-level idea?
Alex: three-stage flow: soft-cordon -> graceful migration/requeue -> hard-evict+replace only if voter consensus persists for N minutes. also add randomized splay to avoid simultaneous mass evacs.
Linh: what counts as a voter? nvidia-smi ECC counters, kernel dmesg Xid logs, hwmon thermal alarms, and our GPU-exporter anomaly score.
Mateo: we should include Slurm job state too — don't want to preempt long-running checkpointed jobs unnecessarily. Slurm hints can allow requeue instead of kill.
Omar: thinking about implementation: a small controller watches the signals, computes a weighted vote, and then emits a decision event. controller calls either k8s cordon/taint or Slurm set node drain depending on node type.
Sasha: edge cases: multi-GPU nodes where only one card flakey. we should prefer isolating the GPU (pci device removal/soft-disable) before whole node evacuation when feasible.
Priya: love the device-isolate-first idea. have we got tooling to unmap a riser/disable GPU without reboot? maybe via nvidia-smi -i <gpu> -pm 0 or kernel quirks.
Alex: prototype commands we've used: ```kubectl cordon ip-10-0-3-45 && kubectl taint nodes ip-10-0-3-45 gpu-health=soft:NoSchedule``` and for slurm: ```scontrol update NodeName=node045 State=drain Reason=\"gpu-health:soft\"```
infra-bot: observed ECC spike: node045 card1 ECC 12 -> 32 within 3m; Xid counter +7 in same window. reporting to /alerts/gpu-health
oncall-bot: auto-note created: incident/2026-03-gpu-vote-node045
Mateo: threshold proposal: soft-cordon when any single voter crosses short window (e.g., ecc > 10/min OR xid > 3 in 5m OR temp > 85C 3x), but only escalate to hard-evict if 2/3 voters persist for 15m.
Linh: add a jittered backoff for repeated cordons: exponential with cap. prevents flapping on noisy telemetry.
Omar: cost angle: we should avoid triggering autoscaler scale-up unnecessarily; controller can mark cordoned nodes as \"degraded\" and let scheduler prefer spare healthy nodes, not immediately request more capacity if jobs can wait short window.
Priya: rollout plan: start with monitoring-only mode (dry-run decisions into logs + dashboard), then opt-in to soft-cordon for a test pool, then enable hard-evict for that pool after 2 weeks of stability.
Alex: metrics to add: decisions_total{outcome=soft,hard,aborted}, voter_scores, time_to_recover, jobs_requeued, eviction_count_by_node, cost_delta_estimate.
Sasha: add an alert for \"mass-splay\" — if >5 nodes cordoned in same AZ within 10m, pause automated evicts and page infra oncall.
Mateo: also tie into model-routing: for hosted inference we can route affected tenants to degraded model pool automatically to keep SLA.
Linh: implement a small consensus config: ```gpu_health.voters = [\"ecc\",\"xid\",\"thermal\",\"exporter\"]
gpu_health.thresholds.soft = {ecc:10,xid:3,temp:85}
gpu_health.thresholds.hard = {consensus:2,window:900}```
Priya: need runbook lines: how to manually clear a soft-cordon, how to force replacement, and how to mark node as quarantined for HW swap. doc stub pls.
Alex: assigned tasks: Linh prototype controller (dry-run) -> 2w, Mateo dashboard visual (voter timelines) -> 1w, Omar integration with autoscaler & splay logic -> 2w, Sasha write runbook -> 3d.
infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-4387 \"gpu health vote evacuation prototype\" and attached dry-run logs.
Omar: one more: ensure controller respects maintenance windows and capacity reservations (dedicated pools) — don't evict nodes that are reserved for enterprise customers unless critical.
Priya: agreed. critical only path should include customer-tag check.
Alex: ok plan looks good. I'll push a design doc today to /docs/infra/gpu-evac-proto and drop a PR link here when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
Mateo: quick note — add a small experiment to test splay: simulate 100 nodes with random faults and assert peak simultaneous evicts < 3%.
Sasha: FYI I'll add a step to the oncall playbook to run diag script when hard-evict fires: gather nvidia-smi -q, dmesg|grep -i xid, and hwmon snapshot.
Linh: cool, I'll include the diag steps in the prototype logs.
Alex: perfect. next sync in infra weekly to review first dry-run outputs.
